title: Linking the Parts of an Essay

sections.content: Every part of an essay needs a link to the next. You already have the tools: *en primer lugar*, *en cuanto a* (B2 Unit 28), *es decir* (B2 Unit 29), *no obstante* and *ahora bien* (B2 Unit 30), *por lo tanto* and *así que* (B2 Unit 31). This lesson adds two phrases for moving a long text forward and a map that shows where each tool belongs.

*Llegados a este punto* means "at this point": it is a participle clause like *terminada la reunión*, which you know from B2 Unit 35, and it says that the text is about to draw on what came before. *En suma* means "in short" and closes a long passage with its main idea.

sections.title: An essay, step by step
rows: En primer lugar, hablaré del precio.
Introduction: say what you will cover.
En cuanto al precio, el plan es caro; no obstante, ofrece ventajas.
Llegados a este punto, conviene hablar del tiempo.
Por lo tanto, el plan es una buena idea.
En suma, el plan merece la pena.

sections.content: Do not start every sentence with a marker: that sounds mechanical. Use one at each real turn of the argument: where you add a point, limit it, move on or close.
